catalog.name: Territorial data
catalog.description: This collection includes information of various kinds complementary to those specifically related to energy. In particular, it contains information on the resident population (at different levels of spatial aggregation, over the years), on risk assessment aspects (seismic risk) as well as information on environmental constraints, particularly useful for analyzing potential territorial limitations to the exploitation and development of RES. These data can be valid inputs to models for the energy planning of the territory.

members.name: Official Protected Area List (EUAP)
members.description: Map of the VI Official List of Protected Natural Areas (EUAP) updated to 2011. Established on the basis of law 394/91 Framework law on protected areas, the official list currently in force is that relating to the 6th Update approved with D.M. 27/04/2010 and published in the Ordinary Supplement n. 115 to the Official Journal no. 125 of 05/31/2010. According to the law 394/91, the protected areas are divided into National Parks (PNZ), Natural Marine Protected Areas (MAR), Marine State Natural Parks (PNZ_m), State Natural Reserves (RNS), Regional Natural Parks and Reserves (PNR - RNR), Submerged Natural Parks (GAPN), Other Protected Natural Areas (AAPN). The list is compiled and periodically updated by the Ministry of the Environment and the Protection of the Territory and the Sea - Nature Protection Directorate. Source: Ministry of Environment Energy Security.

members.name: Sites of Community Importance (SIC)
members.description:
Map of sites of Community Importance and Special Areas of Conservation (ZSC) present in Italy updated in 2023. The Site of Community Importance (SIC) and the Special Conservation Area (ZSC), are concepts defined by the Community Directive n. 43 of 21 May 1992, (92/43/EEC), also known as the \"Habitats\" Directive, and implemented in Italy in 1997. The Directive relates to the conservation of natural and semi-natural habitats and wild flora and fauna.

Source: Ministry of Environment Energy Security.

members.name: Special Protection Areas (ZPS)
members.description:
Map of the Special Protection Areas present on the Italian territory updated in 2023. The Special Protection Areas (ZPS), in Italy, in accordance with art. 1 paragraph 5 of Law No. 157/1992 are protection zones chosen along the bird migration routes, aimed at the maintenance and arrangement of suitable habitats for the conservation and management of migratory wild bird populations. The associated table contains a series of information among which code, denomination, surface, perimeter and Region to which each zone belongs.

Source: Ministry of Environment Energy Security.

members.name: Wetlands (Ramsar)
members.description:
Map of Ramsar areas, areas of the Italian territory that meet the requirements of the international convention relating to wetlands of international importance, especially as a habitat for aquatic birds, known as the Ramsar Convention. The Ramsar Convention is an act signed in Ramsar, Iran, on February 2nd, 1971. The Ramsar Convention was ratified and implemented by Italy with Presidential Decree no. 448 of 13rd March 1976 and with the subsequent Presidential Decree n. 184 of 11th February 1987. According to the Convention are meant for wetlands marshes, peats or basins, natural or artificial, permanent or temporary, with stagnant or flowing water, fresh, brackish or salty, including expanses of sea water the depth of which, at low tide, does not exceed six metres. According to the Convention, waterbirds are birds ecologically dependent on wetlands. Ramsar areas update 2021.

Source: Ministry of Environment Energy Security.

members.name: Important Bird Areas (IBA)
members.description:
Map of Important Bird Areas or IBA, http://wms.pcn.minambiente.it/ogc?map=/ms_ogc/wfs/IBA.map which are areas that play a key role in the protection of birds and biodiversity, the identification of which is part of a worldwide project, managed by BirdLife International. The IBA project was born from the need to identify homogeneous and standardized criteria for the designation of ZPS. The IBAs were used to assess the adequacy of the national networks of designated ZPS in the Member States, 71% of the IBA area is also a ZPS. To be recognized as an IBA, a site must have at least one of the following characteristics: hosting a significant number of individuals of one or more globally threatened species; be part of a type of area that is important for the conservation of particular species (e.g. wetlands); be an area where a particularly large number of migrating birds are concentrated.

Source: Ministry of Environment Energy Security.

members.name: Sea uses
members.description: This collection provides a representation of the main current and planned uses of the sea that may interact with or interfere with the development of offshore wind energy. The data presented include, in particular, the Maritime Spatial Plans developed at the national level, shipping routes, fishing areas, military zones, marine protected areas, and other regulatory or functional constraints. The information, collected from official sources and harmonized on a geographic basis, highlights potential overlaps with areas eligible for offshore wind installations, contributing to a more integrated and sustainable assessment of maritime space use. </br> The objective is to provide a support tool for planning and permitting processes, promoting a coordinated approach between the evaluation of offshore wind potential and other uses and constraints of the sea, in line with shared marine spatial management strategies.

members.name: Maritime spatial planning
members.description:
The map shows the division of the sea into Planning Units (UP), each associated with one or more prevailing uses (priority, reserved, limited, or general), as defined by the Maritime Spatial Plans. The data come from the SID platform – Il portale del mare (https://www.sid.mit.gov.it/) and reflect the official designated uses identified by the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport (MIT), in accordance with European Directive 2014/89/EU.

Data download

members.name: Maritime traffic corridors
members.description:
The map shows the main maritime traffic corridors, in terms of route density (number of routes per km²). The data used are sourced from the EMODnet catalog (https://emodnet.ec.europa.eu/geoviewer/), under the “Human Activities” category, specifically from the “Route Density” data layer, produced by the European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA). The “Route Density” indicator is based on data from the Automatic Identification System (AIS), has a spatial resolution of approximately 1,100 meters, and is available from 2019 onwards with monthly or annual temporal aggregation. The reference year for the data presented here is 2023.

members.name: Fishing activities
members.description:
The map represents the intensity of fishing activities in Italian waters, based on the average annual fishing effort (expressed in hours/km². This parameter is calculated by combining various factors, including the number of vessels operating in an area, time spent fishing, vessel capacity, and the characteristics of the fishing gear used. The data come from the SID platform – Il portale del mare (https://www.sid.mit.gov.it/) and were processed by the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty and Forests (MASAF). They represent, on a regular 3 km grid, the average number of hours spent on fishing activities during the years 2006–2018, filtered and classified to isolate positions corresponding to actual fishing activity (excluding those related to navigation or time spent in port).
